decisions.rationale: "bipolar disorder" names a single defined condition with its own specific definition, so it is treated as a Specific Disease rather than a family-level Disease Class.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Annotate all Specific Disease mentions

decisions.rationale: "bipolar affective disorder" is the full name of the disease studied and refers to one specific disease, so it is a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Annotate all Specific Disease mentions; Rule 5: minimum necessary span

decisions.rationale: "BPAD" is the abbreviation defined in the preceding text as bipolar affective disorder. Abbreviations are annotated as a separate mention referring to the same Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 6: Annotate all synonymous mentions

decisions.rationale: Second occurrence of the abbreviation "BPAD" in the abstract, referring to the same specific disease. Duplicate mentions are annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 4: Annotate duplicate mentions

decisions.rationale: "bipolar and recurrent unipolar" is one contiguous string referring to two separate diseases (bipolar disorder and recurrent unipolar disorder), so it is annotated as a single Composite Mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 2: Annotate contiguous text strings (Composite Mention)

decisions.rationale: "RUP" is the abbreviation for recurrent unipolar disorder and is used to modify the noun phrase "sib pairs", so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3: Disease mentions used as Modifiers for other concepts; What to Annotate 6 (abbreviations)

decisions.rationale: "bipolar and RUP" is a contiguous string containing two separate disease mentions (bipolar and recurrent unipolar), so it is a Composite Mention even though it modifies "sib pairs".
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 2: Annotate contiguous text strings (Composite Mention)

decisions.rationale: Third occurrence of the abbreviation "BPAD" in the text ("linkage of BPAD to chromosome 18"), referring to the same specific disease. Duplicates are annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 4: Annotate duplicate mentions; What to Annotate 6: synonymous mentions

decisions.rationale: "this disorder" is a pronominal reference to the disease with a general noun ("disorder"), not a named disease mention. General terms like "disease", "syndrome" and "deficiency" are excluded.
